items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I became acquainted with Frisco in 35.

ctx.x: Kenny Clarke who had been working in the orchestra of Tony Proto, a french altoist, and Lobo Nochio, a singer, formed an orchestra, and I joined it. Lobo had been in the army, was dischraged in Europe and had settled in Paris. In the orchestra was Byas, James Moody, Hubert Fol, Nat Peck, an American white trombonist, Jay Cameron, another white American, who played baritone sax, Pierre Michelot, a fine French bass player, and a few more French musieians whose names I don't remember. An English girl named Anabella…

We were engaged to work at Frisco's International Bopera House in Montmartre on rue Notre Dame de Lorette. I became acquainted with Frisco in 35. At one time, he had a club in London and had come to France in the 20's. I was not supposed to stay with the orchestra very long because I had been engaged before to go to Nice for two weeks in a place called Club St. Germain des Mers, which was to open in late July by Sarge Griffin and the director of the Edouard 7th theatre. In August, I was to join the orchestra of…

In Nice, I worked with Bernard Peiffer, Huber Fol who had been in the Clarke-Lobo orchestra. Hubert told me that the later orchestra didn't last long because Frisco wanted the French musicians to continue to play when the Americans would take a rest and the place was not going to well as far as business was concerned. Kenny and Lobo did not agree with the way Frisco wanted the band to play and that didn't help either the situation, so the band broke up after a few weeks.
